answer.rationale: Write-path p99 rose ~30 minutes after the new build and has kept climbing through settlement peak, which is more consistent with a progressive release regression than a known daily load step. Rollback is the only candidate that can remove a bad build while still accepting writes; circuit breaking would shed customer writes, failover is unmotivated, and read-replica routing addresses report/read offload not this write-heavy path. Capacity add (b3) remains a plausible alternative if this is pure saturation, so I am verifying b1 and b3 rather than treating either consolidation as decisive. Settlement is in-flight high-value traffic, so the rollback should be staged rather than a fleet-wide cutover, and it is still uncertain whether latency is causal to the release versus peak write contention.
